actions.action: Authorize format access per requesting client.
actions.mechanism: Server-side capability checks, not the flag alone, determine creation and opening eligibility.
actions.implementation: Require enabled creation flag plus declared write capability; require declared read capability for opening. Revalidate session declarations rather than trusting cached account capabilities.
actions.check: Seed a capable account cache, then connect an old client: new-format creation and opening fail; authorized legacy reads succeed.
actions.risk: Incorrect declarations remain possible; fail closed only for new-format operations.

actions.action: Fork legacy documents instead of upgrading them.
actions.mechanism: Separate document identities preserve previously readable content without lossy conversion or in-place format replacement.
actions.implementation: Keep legacy documents and permissions intact. Create an explicitly labeled new-format fork; never redirect legacy identifiers or overwrite their content with incompatible edits.
actions.check: During mixed-version collaboration, a new client edits its fork while an old client successfully reads the unchanged legacy document.
actions.risk: Branches diverge; explicitly disclose that legacy readers do not receive fork updates.

actions.action: Make rollback stop creation, not destroy documents.
actions.mechanism: Separate creation admission from durable storage and the read path for existing new-format documents.
actions.implementation: Rollback disables new-format creation and editing. Retain document bytes, permissions, and format readers; capable clients open existing documents read-only. Leave legacy access unchanged.
actions.check: Create a new-format document, roll back, and verify byte integrity, capable-client reads, rejected writes, and continued old-client legacy reads.
actions.risk: Operational rollback must retain the reader service and compatible storage schema.
